items.question: An order app's entry-slippage guard seeds a chase anchor at placement. A fix just made the anchor reset when the exchange rejects a placement. A gap remains: if code throws between the guard and the send (for example a blank Trigger Offset box makes a parse throw), nothing was sent but the anchor stays seeded, so the next placement can be refused against a stale price. A working order's anchor must not be wiped by a failed second click. What to do?

options.label: (a)
options.text: Fold into the current spec: in the placement routine, reset the anchor at exit only if THIS call seeded it and did not reach the send. A local flag; one reset in a Finally; never touches an anchor seeded by an earlier working order.

options.label: (b)
options.text: Accept: record it; a blank Trigger Offset box is unusual, and the bridge half already reports the real reason.

items.rationale: (a) closes the last path by which a never-sent placement leaves a stale anchor, with a few local lines that cannot affect a working order. (b) leaves a known spurious-refusal path open, and a blank box is exactly the kind of slip that happens.
